question: Should a descendant completion become terminally `delivered` once its requester consumes it, even if the requester’s final external delivery fails afterward?
rationale: This is a lifecycle and user-observable delivery contract, not a mechanical implementation choice: it determines whether later retry and finalization paths may be suppressed.

options.title: Keep consumption as terminal delivery
options.body: Accept requester consumption as the authoritative completion boundary and require runtime proof for outer-send failure, restart, and duplicate-announcement behavior.

options.title: Model consumption separately
options.body: Persist requester consumption as acknowledgement metadata while reserving terminal delivered status for the existing visible-delivery contract.

options.title: Pause this PR
options.body: Defer the accounting change until the broader durable completion-delivery direction has an owner-approved contract.

recommendation.title: Model consumption separately
recommendation.body: Persist requester consumption as acknowledgement metadata while reserving terminal delivered status for the existing visible-delivery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged deterministic announcement work is the closest established ownership signal for the delivery boundary this PR extends.
